summary.short: Gives the UK Competition and Markets Authority powers over digital markets: designating firms with strategic market status, imposing conduct requirements and pro-competition orders, and enforcing them with penalties. It also amends UK competition and merger law. Dated 24 May 2024 in the text.
summary.long: Part 1 (digital markets) lets the CMA designate undertakings with strategic market status in a digital activity linked to the UK, where substantial and entrenched market power, strategic significance and a turnover condition (global turnover over £25 billion or UK turnover over £1 billion) are met; designations last five years (ss 2, 7, 18). Designated undertakings may face conduct requirements, enforcement orders, commitments, a final offer mechanism and pro-competition interventions (ss 19–56), must report certain mergers before completion (ss 57–68), and must name a nominated officer and file compliance reports (ss 83–84). Investigatory powers apply (ss 69–82). Penalties reach 10% of turnover for breaches of orders, conduct requirements and merger duties, 1% of turnover for undertakings failing investigative requirements, and up to £30,000 for individuals; offences carry up to two years' imprisonment (ss 85–98). Part 2 (competition) amends Competition Act 1998 prohibitions, investigation and penalty powers, and Enterprise Act 2002 merger, market study and market investigation rules (ss 119–146). The outline also lists Part 3 (enforcement of consumer protection law) and Chapter 1 of Part 4 and Chapter 2 of Part 5, whose text is not in this part of the document.

notes: This part covers Part 1 (ss.1–118, Digital Markets) and Part 2 Chapters 1–5 (ss.119–146, Competition), ending before the heading of Part 3. Schedules 1–14 are referred to but are not reproduced here, so their amendments are not coded. Editorial footnote markers (F1, F2) appear in ss.11(5) and 107(3). Section 116(6) names the statute as 'Digital Markets, Competition and Consumer Act 2024' (singular 'Consumer'), which differs from the Act's own title. Section 138(5) lists sectoral enactments (e.g., Civil Aviation Act 2012, Electricity Act 1989) that regulations under s.138(2) may amend; these are not coded as individual relations. Entities with no verified identifier have empty lei and ticker strings. Obligations, enforcement and thresholds are not coded here, as only relations, entities and notes were requested for this part. Part 2 of 5 covers ss.147-223, Part 4 Chapter 1 (ss.224-252) and the start of Chapter 2 (ss.253-258); s.258(8) is cut off mid-provision. Schedules and s.330 are in other parts, so cross-references to them are not checked here. CRA 2015 is cited only by abbreviation in this part. Penalty caps differ by regime (£300,000 in s.158(5) and s.182(6); £150,000 in s.168(3)(a); £30,000 in s.198(4)) and are not coded in this section. Empty target_instrument_id means the target is not identified in the registry. Entity lei and ticker are not verifiable from the text and are left empty. Part 3 of 5 covers ss 259 to 340 and Schedules 1 to 7 (Chapters 2 to 4 of Part 4 and Parts 5 and 6). Only relations, entities and notes are coded here; thresholds, obligations, events and enforcement in this part are not coded in this pass. Internal inconsistencies: s.289(9) cites the 2013 Regulations as S.I. 3134/2013, whereas s.279(3) and s.289 elsewhere use S.I. 2013/3134; s.317 names the Digital Markets, Competition and Consumer Act 2024 (no s), while the Act is cited elsewhere as Consumers Act. s.318 provides that Chapter 1 of Part 5 (motor fuel information powers) expires at the end of five years from the day the Act is passed, subject to regulations. Schedule 4 changes merger turnover thresholds (not coded here). Part 4 of 5 covers Schedules 7 (from its Part 1 onward; the Schedule 7 heading is not in this part), 8-18. Schedule 7 Part 3 para 15 refers to paragraph 15 of Schedule 6B and to section 124 of EA 2002; the insertion target is inferred from those references. Internal inconsistency: Sch 13 para 5 refers to the Communications Act 2002, while Sch 12 para 13 and the other provisions concern the Communications Act 2003. Cross-references also vary: Sch 15 Pt 1 and Sch 16 cite Chapters 1-4 of Part 4 of this Act, while Sch 18 paras 6-7 and 11 cite Chapter 3 of Part 3. Schedule 15 and 16 list many further enactments; only examples are recorded as relations, and Schedule 15 para F4-F6 markers show omitted entries with blank text. Entities are limited to bodies named as designated or empowered in this part; firms are not named. Part 5 of 5: the closing paragraphs of a schedule of amendments (paras 11-13) and Schedules 19-30 (transitional provisions, unfair practices list, consequential amendments, excluded contracts, pre-contract information, excluded arrangements, ADR exemptions and accreditation, Sch. 27-30 amendments). Relations list each amended Act once, with the Sch. 30 disclosure amendments summarised rather than separately coded. Target instrument IDs are empty because no registry IDs were supplied. Several Sch. 30 disclosure lists differ: some include Part 1 of this Act (paras 28, 29, 45) and others do not. Entity lei and ticker are empty.
